$comment: Source of truth for PeachPDF's CSS/SVG property dispatch, consumed by PeachPDF.SourceGenerators to emit CssPropertyRegistry.g.cs / SvgPropertyRegistry.g.cs. See CLAUDE.md's generator section for the authoring workflow and the PPGxxx diagnostics that check this file. Every HTML/SVG property PeachPDF's renderer dispatches lives here — see docs/html-css-support.md for the reader-facing compatibility matrix this data backs.

properties.name: border-bottom-width
properties.comment: Accepts a valid length, or the auto keyword (compared case-insensitively — an existing inconsistency vs. most other keyword checks in this codebase, encoded as-is rather than silently fixed).

properties.name: transform
properties.comment: cssDataType 'cssom' keeps real dispatch exactly as permissive as before (matching actual CSS transform-list semantics: a value with one unimplemented function, e.g. perspective(), is still syntactically valid and its implemented functions still apply - see TransformIntegrationTests.Perspective_IsUnsupported_TreatedAsIdentity). supportsDataType 'transform' is the stricter, @supports-only grammar (CssValueParser.IsValidTransformValue): the real set of transform functions BuildFunctionMatrix implements at paint time. perspective() parses as valid CSS but is silently dropped at paint time, so it must not report as @supports-true even though it's still accepted and stored by real dispatch.

properties.name: box-sizing
properties.comment: Replaces the old CssUtils.IsValidBoxSizing helper. CssProperty<BoxSizingMode>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed enum storage instead of a raw string).

properties.name: direction
properties.comment: TrySet/SupportsDeclaration validate the value against Map.DirectionModes' own keys (ltr/rtl, case-insensitive) via the enum-keyword data type; an unrecognized value is rejected. CssProperty<T>.FromCssText itself never rejects once a value reaches the setter — it falls back to the keyword default (ltr) — so the fallback only applies to a value that already passed validation upstream. The svg binding is a carrier-only, hand-written entry (applyIn: manual) — SVG never stores direction on SvgElement, only threads it through SvgInheritedPaint for text runs, so it is deliberately excluded from the generated SVG dispatch (see SvgTreeBuilder.ApplyCommon's manual-property section).

properties.name: page-break-after
properties.comment: Legacy alias of break-after (css-break-3 §3.3), sharing its storage; the CSS2.1 'always' keyword remaps to break-after's 'page'.

properties.name: font-family
properties.comment: Multi-field write: the resolved family (FontFamily) and the raw authored list (FontFamilyList) both come from one declaration. The initial value is UA/platform-defined (DefaultFontResolver.DefaultFont is computed per-platform at runtime), hence an {expression} rather than a string literal.

properties.name: margin-block-start
properties.comment: CSS Logical Properties (css-logical-1) resolution scratch space — CssBox.LogicalProperties.cs. Read exactly once by CssBox.ResolveLogicalProperties, which maps it to one of margin-top/-right/-bottom/-left depending on this box's own resolved direction/writing-mode; that cross-property resolution stays hand-written (a single JSON entry cannot express a function of two other properties' resolved values). No initial value by design: the physical property it resolves into already has one. Validation mirrors margin-top's (none).

properties.name: overflow-wrap
properties.comment: Grammar accepted by Layer A, deliberately unimplemented by Layer B (docs/html-css-support.md). TrySet/SupportsDeclaration correctly return false, replacing the old CssUtils dispatch's silent no-op lambda. inherited: false and initialValue: null both preserve today's actual behavior (CssDefaults never listed it as inherited, despite CSS Text 4 §3 specifying inheritance for it) rather than silently fixing a spec deviation this migration isn't scoped to touch.

properties.name: fill
properties.comment: SVG <paint> (svg-shapes-1.1 §13.2): none | url(#id) | currentColor | <color>. Produces a structured SvgPaint, not a string, so it needs its own data type rather than HTML's plain 'color'. No customSetter needed — the generated default svg-paint setter already reclassifies a url() reference from gradient to pattern against the current document's id registries via ctx.ResolveUrlPaintKind (SvgTreeBuilder.ResolveUrlPaintKind bound as a delegate); SvgValueParsers.TryParsePaint has no document context of its own and always classifies url(#id) as GradientRef.

properties.name: stroke
properties.comment: Same SVG <paint> grammar and url()-reclassification need as fill (see its comment) — stroke just targets a different SvgElement field and a different initial value/inherited carrier.

properties.name: stroke-width
properties.comment: SVG <length> (svg-strokeprops-1.1 §11.4), percentages resolved against the viewport diagonal via ctx.ViewportDiagonal. Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value, matching SvgTreeBuilder.ApplyCommon's existing '?? inherited.StrokeWidth' behavior.

properties.name: stroke-miterlimit
properties.comment: SVG <number> (svg-strokeprops-1.1 §11.4), parsed via the shared SvgValueParsers.ParseLength grammar with no reference length (a plain unitless number is what the spec actually allows here, and ParseLength already accepts a bare number). Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value.

properties.name: stroke-dashoffset
properties.comment: SVG <length> (svg-strokeprops-1.1 §11.4), percentages resolved against the viewport diagonal. Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value.

properties.name: stroke-dasharray
properties.comment: SVG <length># | none (svg-strokeprops-1.1 §11.4) — SvgValueParsers.ParseDashArray already returns null (invalid) vs. an array, so this is its own data type (svg-length-list) rather than a plain length. Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value.

properties.name: fill-rule
properties.comment: Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value (invalidBehavior: inherit), per SVG 1.1 §11.4 — see #599; SvgTreeBuilder.ApplyCommon checks TrySet's return value and assigns inherited.FillRule on failure, the same shape stroke-width/etc. use. supportedValues/keywordComparison document the real grammar; customValidator/customSetter reuse the shared TryParseFillRule parser directly rather than re-deriving a keyword→enum mapping (customSetter code runs only after Validate_FillRule already passed, so the second TryParseFillRule call here can never itself fail).

properties.name: fill-opacity
properties.comment: Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value (invalidBehavior: inherit), per SVG 1.1 §11.4 — see #675; SvgTreeBuilder.ApplyCommon checks TrySet's return value and assigns inherited.FillOpacity on failure, the same shape stroke-width/etc. use.

properties.name: stroke-opacity
properties.comment: Same shape as fill-opacity (see its comment) — see #675.

properties.name: stroke-linecap
properties.comment: Falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value (invalidBehavior: inherit), per SVG 1.1 §11.4 — see #599; SvgTreeBuilder.ApplyCommon checks TrySet's return value and assigns inherited.StrokeLineCap on failure, the same shape stroke-width/etc. use. customValidator/customSetter reuse the shared TryParseLineCap parser directly (see the fill-rule entry's identical note) instead of the inline enum-mapping switch this entry used before the SVG cutover.

properties.name: stroke-linejoin
properties.comment: Same shape as stroke-linecap (see its comment) — falls back to the inherited value on an invalid value (invalidBehavior: inherit), per SVG 1.1 §11.4 — see #599.

properties.name: outline-width
properties.comment: thin/medium/thick are real <line-width> keywords (CSS-UI-4 §4). An authored value (e.g. "outline-width: thin") never reaches this layer as the literal keyword - the CSS-OM's LineWidthConverter already resolves it to a literal px Length, and Property.Value serializes that resolved length, so Validate_OutlineWidth only ever sees e.g. "1px" (which the plain "length" clause already accepts). These three keywords are listed here for the *initial-value* defaulting path instead: DomParser.CascadeApplyStyles re-applies each property's literal css-properties.json initialValue ("medium" here) via CssUtils.SetPropertyValue every cascade pass, which - unlike the record's own C# default field initializer - does run through this same Validate_OutlineWidth gate.

properties.name: opacity
properties.comment: customValidator implements <alpha-value> (css-color-4 §14): a plain number or a percentage, matching CssValueParser.ParseNumber's actual grammar (which the html setter's ActualOpacity resolution calls) rather than the cssDataType 'number' clause alone, which doesn't accept a percentage.

properties.name: -peachpdf-pdf-form-field
properties.comment: PeachPDF's PDF-output extension for interactive form fields (no W3C spec - see issue #709). auto infers the field kind from the element (tag name + <input type=>) via FormFieldMapper.Classify; text/checkbox/radio/select force a kind regardless of the element's own type. Inert unless PdfGenerateConfig.EnableInteractivePdfForms is set, and only ever applies to a real <input>/<select> element - a declaration on any other element is simply ignored. cssom/string-stored, like -peachpdf-pdf-tag-type - FormFieldMapper re-resolves the raw string via Map.PdfFormFieldKinds.

properties.name: -peachpdf-pdf-form-field-auto-font-size
properties.comment: PeachPDF's own spelling of Prince's -prince-pdf-form-field-settings 'auto-font-size' sub-option (see the shorthand's own entry) - when auto, a generated text field's /DA font size is written as 0 (PDF's own auto-size convention) instead of a fixed size. Only meaningful when the element also classifies to a text field.

properties.name: -peachpdf-pdf-form-field-comb
properties.comment: PeachPDF's own spelling of Prince's -prince-pdf-form-field-settings 'comb(<integer>)' sub-option (see the shorthand's own entry) - none | <integer>, the number of evenly-spaced character cells. Sets the PDF field flag bit Comb and /MaxLen. Only meaningful when the element also classifies to a text field.

properties.name: -peachpdf-pdf-form-field-do-not-scroll
properties.comment: PeachPDF's own spelling of Prince's -prince-pdf-form-field-settings 'do-not-scroll' sub-option (see the shorthand's own entry) - sets the PDF field flag bit DoNotScroll. No appearance-stream effect, just a flag PDF readers use for their own editing UI. Only meaningful when the element also classifies to a text field.

properties.name: bookmark-level
properties.comment: CSS Generated Content Module Level 3 §2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-content-3/#bookmark-level). cssom/string-stored, like -peachpdf-pdf-tag-type - BookmarkOutlineBuilder parses the raw none/<integer> string itself (mirroring StructureTagMapper.Classify's own re-parse of PdfTagType), since the CSS-OM BookmarkLevelProperty converter (Converters.BookmarkLevelConverter) already validates the grammar at declaration time. h1-h6 default to 1-6 via CssDefaults.cs's UA stylesheet, everything else defaults to none (this property's own initial value), which is itself the zero-config "no bookmarks" state.

properties.name: bookmark-label
properties.comment: CSS Generated Content Module Level 3 §2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-content-3/#bookmark-label). A <content-list> - the same string/counter()/attr()/content()/string() grammar `content` accepts, minus url()/gradients (image content, not applicable to a label) and the quote-modes/element() (meaningful only within flowing generated content, not a standalone label string) - see the shared Converters.ContentListItemConverter both properties' CSS-OM converters reference, and CssContentEngine.ResolveContentTokens/ResolveBookmarkLabel for the shared resolver. Initial value content(text) means "the element's own rendered text", resolved via the same content()/"text" branch content() itself uses.

properties.name: bookmark-state
properties.comment: CSS Generated Content Module Level 3 §2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/css-content-3/#bookmark-state). cssom/string-stored, like bookmark-level - BookmarkOutlineBuilder parses the raw open/closed string itself via Map.BookmarkStates.

properties.name: -peachpdf-bookmark-target
properties.comment: NOT a css-content-3 property - css-content-3 defines only bookmark-level/-label/-state (verified against the spec source directly; an earlier draft of this issue assumed bookmark-target was part of the same spec and it is not). This is Prince's own extension (prince-bookmark-target, self | url() | attr(), default self) - PeachPDF's own documented spelling follows the -peachpdf-pdf-tag-type precedent for a PDF-output feature with no real spec-track name, rather than the unprefixed spelling Prince itself uses. See BookmarkOutlineBuilder.ResolveTargetValue for self/url()/attr() resolution and the in-document-fragment-vs-external-URL split.

properties.name: -prince-bookmark-level
properties.comment: Hidden, undocumented compat alias for Prince's own -prince-bookmark-level spelling (Prince documents both an unprefixed and a -prince- prefixed form for all four bookmark-* properties) - translates to the real spec property bookmark-level at parse time. Not documented in docs/, same pattern as the other PDF-output extensions' Prince/prefixed compat shims.

properties.name: -prince-bookmark-label
properties.comment: Hidden, undocumented compat alias for Prince's own -prince-bookmark-label spelling - translates to the real spec property bookmark-label at parse time.

properties.name: -prince-bookmark-state
properties.comment: Hidden, undocumented compat alias for Prince's own -prince-bookmark-state spelling - translates to the real spec property bookmark-state at parse time.

properties.name: -prince-bookmark-target
properties.comment: Hidden, undocumented compat alias for Prince's own -prince-bookmark-target spelling - translates to -peachpdf-bookmark-target (a PeachPDF extension, not a real spec property - see that entry) at parse time.

properties.name: bookmark-target
properties.comment: Hidden, undocumented compat alias for Prince's own bookmark-target spelling (Prince's convenience alias for its prince-bookmark-target extension) - translates to -peachpdf-bookmark-target at parse time. The one place in this file an unprefixed name is NOT a real spec property: css-content-3 defines no bookmark-target at all (see -peachpdf-bookmark-target's own comment).

properties.name: margin-bottom
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: margin-left
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: margin-right
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: margin-top
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: left
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: top
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: right
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: bottom
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: break-before
properties.comment: cssDataType's own supportedValues includes region/avoid-region because real dispatch stores any css-break-4-valid keyword (CssUtilsTests.Cascade_BreakBefore_StoresOnlySpecValues) even though BreakValues.cs's fragmentation logic doesn't act on them - no FragmentationContext.Region exists, consistent with this repo's lack of multi-column-region support. supportsDataType is the stricter, @supports-only list excluding region/avoid-region for exactly that reason.

properties.name: break-inside
properties.comment: avoid-region is stored (real dispatch) like break-before/-after's region/avoid-region, but excluded from supportsDataType's stricter @supports-only list for the same reason - see break-before's comment.

properties.name: break-after
properties.comment: cssDataType's own supportedValues includes region/avoid-region because real dispatch stores any css-break-4-valid keyword (CssUtilsTests.Cascade_BreakBefore_StoresOnlySpecValues) even though BreakValues.cs's fragmentation logic doesn't act on them - no FragmentationContext.Region exists, consistent with this repo's lack of multi-column-region support. supportsDataType is the stricter, @supports-only list excluding region/avoid-region for exactly that reason.

properties.name: page-break-before
properties.comment: Legacy alias of break-before (css-break-3 §3.3); the CSS2.1 'always' keyword remaps to break-before's 'page'.

properties.name: page-break-inside
properties.comment: Legacy alias of break-inside, sharing its storage - no value remap on this axis.

properties.name: box-decoration-break
properties.comment: CssProperty<BoxDecorationBreakMode>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed enum storage instead of a raw string).

properties.name: background-image
properties.comment: Parses into a structurally different field (image list) via a custom setter; cssDataType 'cssom' delegates grammar validation to the CSS-OM's own BackgroundImageProperty.

properties.name: container-type
properties.comment: CSS Containment 3 SS2. Establishes this box as a query container for @container: 'size' contains both axes (inline + block), 'inline-size' only the inline axis, 'normal' establishes no size query container (but still a style-query container - see CssBox.FindNearestQueryContainer's QueryKind.Style branch). Not inherited.

properties.name: container-name
properties.comment: CSS Containment 3 SS2. Raw space-separated <custom-ident>+ list (or 'none'), stored as text - PeachPDF.CSS.ContainerNameProperty does not yet validate full custom-ident grammar (an existing simplification), so this delegates to it rather than re-deriving a second parser (see CLAUDE.md's 'one parser' rule). Splitting on whitespace and matching against an @container rule's queried name happens at container-resolution time (CssBox.FindNearestQueryContainer), not here.

properties.name: position
properties.comment: Multi-field write, mirroring font-family's precedent: css-gcpm-3 extends the keyword grammar with a running(<custom-ident>) function form, which the plain enum-keyword data type can't express. customValidator/customSetter delegate to the shared PositionValueGrammar.TryParse (also used by the CSS-OM PositionProperty converter's RunningFunctionConverter) so the two never independently re-derive the grammar; the resolved custom-ident is stored on the hand-written CssBox.RunningElementName companion field (see ComputedStyleAreas.cs's DisplayPositioningArea partial), not in this enum.

properties.name: overflow
properties.comment: 'clip' is intentionally excluded - CssUtilsTests/MonolithicContentTests confirm it isn't (and wasn't, pre-migration) an accepted value, so it never overrides the inherited/initial 'visible' and MonolithicContent.IsScrollContainer sees 'visible', not a stored 'clip'. 'auto'/'scroll' are genuinely used by MonolithicContent.IsScrollContainer (a non-visible overflow makes a box a scroll container, treated as monolithic/unbreakable across pages) even though they don't distinguish real interactive scrolling from 'hidden' - both are meaningful CSS Overflow 3 values for a non-interactive, paginated renderer.

properties.name: z-index
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, int>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: line-height
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<NormalKeyword, LengthOrUnitless>-backed (issue #598's follow-up) - the tenth and final keyword-or-value batch. Fixes a real pre-existing bug along the way: a bare unitless multiplier (e.g. 'line-height: 1.5') previously validated but silently collapsed ActualLineHeight to 0 (the old string-based ParseLength had no case for a number with no unit token); LengthOrUnitless's Unitless side now resolves it correctly (CSS2.1 §10.8.1: the number times the element's own font size). 'auto' is deliberately not in supportedValues - CSS Inline Layout 3's grammar is 'normal | <number> | <length-percentage>', auto was never part of it.

properties.name: vertical-align
properties.comment: CSS 2.1 §10.8.1 also accepts a <percentage>/<length> value form, offsetting the box from its own baseline (issue #603) - the value side reuses word-spacing/line-height's LengthOrCalc plumbing (valueType "length" already covers percentages via CssValueParser.IsValidLength/ValueExtensions.ToDistance, no separate percentage data type needed). PeachBaselineMiddle (the deprecated img align=middle sentinel, see Keywords.PeachBaselineMiddle) is never produced by this grammar - DomParser assigns it directly via CssKeywordOrValueParser's keyword side, same as Float's img align handling.

properties.name: text-transform
properties.comment: cssDataType's own Map.TextTransforms includes full-width, mapped to CssBox.cs's ApplyTextTransform which converts characters to their Unicode fullwidth compatibility form. full-size-kana is not implemented (not in the TextTransform enum or Map.TextTransforms) so it's rejected outright and excluded from supportsSupportedValues below, same shape as word-break's keep-all split.

properties.name: word-break
properties.comment: cssDataType's own Map.WordBreaks includes keep-all because Layer A's own WordBreakConverter/Map.WordBreaks parses and stores it as valid CSS (WordBreak.KeepAll), even though CssBox.cs's line-breaking logic only special-cases break-all - keep-all has no distinct effect (see .claude/accepted-gaps/word-break-keep-all-no-effect.md). supportsDataType is the stricter, @supports-only list excluding keep-all for exactly that reason, same shape as break-before's region/avoid-region split.

properties.name: word-spacing
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<NormalKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText. The eager em-to-pt resolution (valueComputation "no-ems") that used to run in the CssBox setter now runs in RegistryEmitter.BuildHtmlAssignment against the raw text before FromCssText parses it — see StylePropertiesEmitter's doc comment.

properties.name: letter-spacing
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<NormalKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up). Same no-ems eager em-resolution as word-spacing — see its comment.

properties.name: text-decoration-color
properties.comment: Real color grammar now validated (was previously a documented gap: no color validation despite being a color property).

properties.name: font-size
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<FontSizeKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText. supportedValues (via FontSizeKeyword/Map.FontSizeKeywords) deliberately excludes CSS Fonts 4's xxx-large - FontSizeResolver.Resolve's switch has no case for it, so an accepted 'font-size: xxx-large' would fall through to the length/calc() value path (which can't parse the bare keyword), Math.Max(0, ...)-clamp to 0, and silently render invisible text rather than being rejected. RegistryEmitter.BuildHtmlAssignment runs CssBox.ResolveFontSizeValueComputation(value) (the html.valueComputation "font-size" case) against the raw authored text before FromCssText parses it - see that method's own doc comment for the eager em/ex/percent/smaller/larger-to-points resolution it performs (calc() and rem stay lazy, resolved later by FontSizeResolver.Resolve/DerivedStyle.ActualFont via LengthOrCalc's deferred-calc mechanism).

properties.name: font-weight
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<FontWeightKeyword, int>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText. CSS Fonts 4's <number> form is validated as a plain integer in [1,1000] (min/max below), not a fractional number — matches ValueExtensions.IsWeight's own range on the Layer A CSS-OM side (issue #655).

properties.name: font-stretch
properties.comment: CssProperty<FontStretch>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed enum storage instead of a raw string) - reuses the pre-existing FontStretch enum/Map.FontStretches map, already used by FontStretchResolver/the legacy CSS-OM layer.

properties.name: list-style-type
properties.comment: cssDataType 'cssom' delegates grammar validation to the CSS-OM's own ListStyleTypeProperty (Converters.ListStyleConverter / Map.ListStyles) - the full predefined-counter-style keyword set plus a literal <string> marker - rather than re-deriving a second, independently-maintained keyword list here (this repo's 'one parser' rule). CssCounterEngine/CommonUtils.ConvertToAlphaNumber and CssBoxMarker.ResolveDefaultContent are the downstream consumers that turn a stored keyword or quoted-string value into an actual marker.

properties.name: list-style-image
properties.comment: Parses into a structured field via a custom setter; cssDataType 'cssom' delegates grammar validation to the CSS-OM's own ListStyleImageProperty.

properties.name: justify-content
properties.comment: Map.JustifyContentKeywords carries the full CSS Box Alignment 3 <content-distribution>/<content-position> grammar - CssLayoutEngineFlex.ComputeMainOffsets and CssLayoutEngineGrid.PositionTracks dispatch every keyword here (issue #645).

properties.name: align-items
properties.comment: Map.AlignItemKeywords carries the full <self-position> grammar including self-start (issue #644) - CssLayoutEngineFlex.ComputeCrossOffsets and CssLayoutEngineGrid.AlignmentOffset both dispatch it. align-items serves both flex and grid layout modes and this entry can't tell which one a given box uses.

properties.name: align-content
properties.comment: Map.AlignContentKeywords carries the full CSS Box Alignment 3 <content-distribution>/<content-position> grammar including start/baseline (issue #645) - CssLayoutEngineFlex.DistributeCrossSpace and CssLayoutEngineGrid.PositionTracks both fall back to their existing start-packing default for start/baseline, which is spec-correct (baseline's content-distribution fallback alignment is start, CSS Box Alignment 3 §8.3).

properties.name: flex-grow
properties.comment: customValidator rejects a negative <number> - css-flexbox-1 §7.1.1 defines flex-grow as a non-negative number, and CssLayoutEngineFlex.cs sums ParseFloat(box.FlexGrow) directly into free-space distribution math with no clamp, so an accepted negative value would corrupt that calculation rather than being merely inert.

properties.name: flex-shrink
properties.comment: customValidator rejects a negative <number> - css-flexbox-1 §7.1.2 defines flex-shrink as a non-negative number, and CssLayoutEngineFlex.cs multiplies ParseFloat(box.FlexShrink) directly into shrink-factor math with no clamp, so an accepted negative value would corrupt that calculation rather than being merely inert.

properties.name: flex-basis
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<FlexBasisKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: align-self
properties.comment: Same enum/keyword set as align-items (see its own comment), plus 'auto' (Map.AlignSelfKeywords adds it to Map.AlignItemKeywords) - 'auto' defers to the container's align-items, resolved ad hoc at every read site in CssLayoutEngineFlex.ComputeCrossOffsets/CssLayoutEngineGrid.ResolveSelfAlignment rather than a DerivedStyle accessor.

properties.name: row-gap
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<NormalKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText.

properties.name: column-gap
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<NormalKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up). See CssLayoutEngineColumns.ResolveColumns for multicol's spec-mandated 'normal' => 1em special case (flex/grid instead resolve 'normal' to 0) — unaffected by this storage change, just a call-site consumption detail to preserve.

properties.name: grid-template-columns
properties.comment: cssDataType 'cssom' delegates grammar validation to the CSS-OM's own GridTemplateColumnsProperty; the string setter itself is unconditional once that validation passes. TrySetTypedPropertyValue's existing hand-written _typedPropertySetters entry for this property is unaffected by this migration and is not yet superseded by a generated typed dispatch — a tracked follow-up, not a regression.

properties.name: grid-template-rows
properties.comment: cssDataType 'cssom' delegates grammar validation to the CSS-OM's own GridTemplateRowsProperty; the string setter itself is unconditional once that validation passes. TrySetTypedPropertyValue's existing hand-written _typedPropertySetters entry for this property is unaffected by this migration and is not yet superseded by a generated typed dispatch — a tracked follow-up, not a regression.

properties.name: justify-self
properties.comment: Same enum/keyword set as justify-items, plus 'auto' (Map.JustifySelfKeywords adds it to Map.JustifyItemKeywords) - 'auto' defers to the container's justify-items, resolved ad hoc via CssLayoutEngineGrid.ResolveSelfAlignment (justify-self has no meaning in flex layout).

properties.name: column-count
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, int>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText. Unlike z-index (this mechanism's pilot, whose <integer> is unconstrained), column-count's <integer> must be >= 1 (CSS Multi-column Layout 1 - 0/negative is invalid); min narrows the keyword-or-value grammar's integer clause the same way plain "integer" entries' own min does (see KeywordOrValueGrammar).

properties.name: column-width
properties.comment: CssKeywordOrValue<AutoKeyword, LengthOrCalc>-backed (issue #598's follow-up: typed union storage instead of a raw string) — see CssKeywordOrValueParser.FromCssText. Reuses word-spacing/letter-spacing/row-gap/column-gap's LengthOrCalc value side so a relative-unit calc() still evaluates lazily at consumption time instead of being rejected.
